Lead story · Working better together

Building a stronger handoff, one project at a time

Good engineering depends on more than great individual work. It depends on what happens when that work moves from one team to the next.

This month, project teams at Northstar have been comparing notes on a familiar challenge: how to keep decisions, assumptions and open questions visible as a project moves from design to delivery. The takeaway is refreshingly practical: a clear handoff is a conversation, not just a folder of files.

Teams are trying a simple shared checklist that captures the latest design decisions, outstanding risks, owners and next steps. The goal is not another layer of process; it is fewer surprises, faster answers and more time for the work that matters.

Try it on your next project: before a handoff, spend 15 minutes with the receiving team reviewing what has changed, what remains uncertain and who can help. Small habits can make a big difference across a 200-person firm.
